title: An Atlas proposal may not include language preventing other proposals from editing the same component
content:
A.1.11.2.5.1 is a single-sentence prohibition with large consequences: "Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposals cannot include language that aims to prevent other Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposals from editing the same component of the Atlas within the same Governance Cycle."

Without this rule, the amendment process would be trivially capturable. A proposer could attach an exclusivity clause to any edit and thereby convert a normal proposal into a lock on that part of the Atlas — blocking rival amendments not by winning the argument but by claiming the component first. Repeated across enough components, that turns first-mover advantage into agenda control over the constitution.

Banning the clause preserves genuine competition between simultaneous proposals, and forces the resulting collisions into the open where A.1.11.2.5.2's Reconciliation Process resolves them — either by merging compatible edits or by putting the incompatible ones back to voters.

The generalizable principle: a procedural system must forbid proposals that alter the procedure for handling proposals. Otherwise every substantive contest can be pre-empted by a meta-level move, and the rules become an object of competition rather than its arena.
description: Sky forbids exclusivity clauses outright, so no proposal can lock a component against competing amendments within the same Governance Cycle.
